summary: This bill amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to require all households to meet specific income and resource criteria to be eligible for benefits, thereby closing a loophole that allowed some households to receive nominal benefits without meeting these requirements.

scores.thoughts: This bill aims to close a loophole in the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, which would likely reduce the number of households eligible for benefits. This reduction in eligibility would lead to less government spending on food assistance programs.

The bill directly targets the Food and Nutrition Act, which is a core component of the social safety net. By closing the 'nominal benefits loophole' and requiring all households to meet income and resource criteria, it restricts access to welfare benefits, thus reducing the scope of the social safety net.

The bill tightens SNAP eligibility by closing the nominal benefits loophole, directly reducing the number of households (especially higher-income ones) that can receive benefits and thereby lowering federal spending.
